content: The oral microbiota product contains bacterial spores. The co-administration of antibacterial agents may reduce the efficacy of this product due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is recommended to complete any ongoing antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days prior to initiating treatment with oral microbiota. Specific antibacterial agents, such as erythromycin stearate, fidaxomicin, fosfomycin, gemifloxacin, gentamicin, iclaprim, imipenem/cilastatin, imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam, kanamycin, lefamulin, levofloxacin, lincomycin, linezolid, meropenem, meropenem/vaborbactam, methenamine, methenamine/sodium salicylate/benzoic acid, metronidazole vaginal, minocycline, moxifloxacin, nafcillin, neomycin PO, nitrofurantoin, norfloxacin, ofloxacin, omadacycline, oritavancin, oxacillin, penicillin G aqueous, penicillin G benzathine, penicillin G procaine, penicillin VK, piperacillin, plazomicin, polymyxin B, quinupristin/dalfopristin, relebactam, retapamulin, rifamycin, rifaximin, sarecycline, streptomycin, sulbactam/durlobactam, sulfadiazine, sulfanilamide, and sulfisoxazole, have been identified to decrease the effects of oral microbiota through pharmacodynamic antagonism. In such cases, it is advised to avoid these agents or use alternative drugs to ensure the efficacy of the oral microbiota product.
